info.description: What a program on the user's own machine (a local assistant, a script) reads and writes in the wiki: a page's Markdown, whole or a section at a time, its table of contents, its attachments, the listing of the spaces and their pages, and the search. Every request signs in with an API key of the user's (Authorization: Bearer, or X-API-Key) or with the user's login and password (HTTP Basic), and acts as the user: the spaces' permissions apply as they are. A key's right narrows what the user may do: read allows GET and HEAD, write the rest too. The session's cookie is never read here. Every refusal is JSON, {"error": name, "message": why}. The wiki's MCP server, for assistants, is at /mcp (POST, JSON-RPC over HTTP, signed in by a key as Bearer); it is not described here, as it is no REST API.

A name is taken exactly as sent and never changed. The upload replaces a file of the same name, in its place, only over the version read: If-Match with its ETag replaces it (200), If-None-Match: * attaches only where there is none, and without either a taken name is refused (428). The page's text and its history do not change: write the answer's markdown into the page to show the file.

put.description: The body becomes the page's whole Markdown, as a save in the editor: a new version in the history under the user's name, the change pushed to everyone with the page open, the same notifications; the title stays. Where there is no page, the PUT creates one, as the wiki's New page does: the address's last slug is its slug, and the slugs before it name the page above it, which has to exist. With section or top, the body takes the place of that part of the page alone, and the rest of the page stays as it is; the server ends the body with a line break when it has none. If-Match with the version from the ETag makes the write conditional: a page saved since is refused, and nothing is written. Without it, the write goes over whatever is there, and a part is written in the page as it is when the request comes.

The address spans several segments, and may be sent with its slashes escaped (team%2Fprojects%2Fp%2Fthe-wiki%2F), as a client generated from this document sends a path parameter.
